atoms.text: Nancy goes to the supermarket and buys two aubergines (𝘢), one broccoli (𝘣) and one cauliflower (𝘤).
atoms.sound: Nancy goes to the supermarket and buys two aubergines, one broccoli and one cauliflower.

instruction.text: The total price of all the vegetables is £4. Write an equation to show this information.
If cauliflowers cost £1.40, which of the following equations is correct?
What can this equation then be simplified to?

instruction.text: Use the additional information below to work out the only possible pair of prices for aubergines and broccoli.

atoms.a:
Aubergines are cheaper than broccoli.

The total price of one aubergine and one broccoli is less than £2.
